title: From VLM/VLA's to Embodied Agents — Armen Aghajanyan, Perceptron AI
talk_summary: Armen Aghajanyan of Perceptron AI argues for unifying VLM/VLA/world-model distinctions into 'embodied foundation models' that jointly do perception, reasoning, and control, and describes two research problems: sparse training signal in video and context bloat. He presents a data-sparse mixture-of-experts router that lets the model learn which tokens to skip, and a scaling law trading 10x video pretraining for 10x less teleop data.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of hardcoding which tokens matter or averaging patches, they put a router in the model that predicts which input tokens to skip, learned end-to-end across layers, so compute is allocated to task-relevant tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let the model figure out what tokens it should look at and what tokens it shouldn't look like
takeaways.numbers: patch-averaging hacks gave up to 10x compression; their learned router does it 'for free through all the different layers'

takeaways.what_they_do: They separate an 'embodied reasoning' orchestrator model that decomposes a multi-minute task into subtasks from a fast tactile control policy running underneath, rather than forcing one end-to-end model to do everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can have an orchestrator model that breaks up this tasks into subtasks and there's a tactile control policy that's running on top

takeaways.what_they_do: They run video annotation and self-verification loops on their own cheap AR model because it's fast and orders of magnitude cheaper than Gemini, making iterative self-checking economically viable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you try to do this with Gemini, this video would probably cost you a couple of dollars where for us, it's probably in the sense
takeaways.numbers: ~15x cheaper than Gemini 3.1 Pro claimed for their model

takeaways.technique: Targeted data distribution for a specific capability
takeaways.what_they_do: They beat Gemini's embodied-reasoning model with less compute by deliberately curating training data for a concrete capability (e.g. left/right spatial relations) that internet crawls don't label, rather than relying on scale alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: really thinking about data distributions early on gives you this ability relatively quickly
takeaways.numbers: surpassed Gemini ER 'with relatively less compute'

takeaways.what_they_do: During training they inject fake perturbations (camera off, sunlight from a direction) so the policy doesn't overfit to one environment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do actually, you know, fake um I don't know um one of the one of the arm cameras being off

takeaways.what_they_do: For long video they think about compressing context by distinguishing key frames from delta frames rather than ingesting every frame at high FPS.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do I think about like uh uh key frames versus delta frames? How can I manage my context by training these two off?
takeaways.numbers: models have 1M context but high-FPS video still overflows it
